A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EgoAgent and contain complete, readable main text and supplementary material. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, tables, figures, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original prediction, classification, and TriFinger simulation results in Tables 1–3, plus supplementary OpenSora experiments and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including EgoAgent evaluations, ablations, supplementary OpenSora experiments, and qualitative predictions.

M1.justification: The interleaved causal transformer, predictor/EMA observer, projection and prediction heads, three losses, and inference procedures remain unchanged. Revised query-token and observer descriptions explain the existing method.

E1.justification: Training remains on WalkingTours and Ego-Exo4D. Evaluation retains Ego-Exo4D state and motion prediction, ImageNet-100/1K classification, and TriFinger reach/move-cube tasks. The supplementary scenes and tasks also match.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain VIP, R3M, DINO, DoRA and retrained DoRA, Diffusion Policy-C/T, HumanMAC, and siMLPe. TriFinger retains its DINO/DoRA comparators, and supplementary comparisons retain OpenSora.

E3.justification: Splits, frame sampling, model sizes, training budgets, metrics, and downstream evaluation settings match. Section 4.2 newly specifies that EgoAgent retains the current state in its retrieval gallery; this clarifies previously underdocumented behavior without establishing a protocol revision.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 retains the same loss-removal, single-task, and VQGAN ablations. Action-conditioned retrieval, supplementary OpenSora finetuning and layer/noise analyses, the minimal-motion case study, and attention-map analysis are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Averaging retrieval performance across four timesteps remains unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in the main and supplementary result tables match. For example, EgoAgent-1B retains 46.43 Top1 accuracy and 61.96 mAP for state prediction; supplementary OpenSora middle-layer classification at timestep 128 retains 38.08 Top1 and 64.16 Top5. Qualitative examples and findings also match.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and the task-specific mathematical formulations remain equivalent. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added; the new gradient-conflict discussion is qualitative.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: jointly learning representation, future-state prediction, and 3D actions through interleaving and JEAP, with superior benchmark performance. Rewording does not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 adds a mechanism explanation that query-based separation prevents conflicting gradient updates and permits EMA updates despite the observer lacking action inputs. Existing result interpretations and future-work boundaries concerning detailed hands and long-term memory remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 promises a code/model release without a location; v3 specifies a GitHub repository while retaining future-tense availability. v3 also explicitly states that observer EMA updates include the MLPs and that EgoAgent retains the current state in the retrieval gallery.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly positions EgoAgent as a reactive agent. Background citations to Su et al.'s domain-normalization work and Xue et al.'s pedestrian predictor are replaced by ResNet and Yuan/Kitani's ego-pose forecasting. The supplement adds RoFormer and RMSNorm references; many other bibliography edits update retained works' publication details.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the abstract and selected motivation/method paragraphs, refines grammar and terminology elsewhere, and adds acknowledgments. The main section order, narrative organization, and supplementary structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 receives graphic-sizing refinements, Figure 2's caption gains explicit time indices, and table captions and labels are tidied. Text and tables undergo modest reflow, while the same scientific figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 reduces ambiguity about causal query placement, observer/MLP EMA updates, and the retrieval gallery, and specifies the intended code/model release location. These changes improve readability and reproducibility documentation. The method, experiments, and supporting results remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
